title: regional-soft-anchor-capacity-escrow-routing-policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
We observe two operational gaps during region-level capacity pressure: (1) aggressive cross-region failover that sharply increases tail latency for downstream regions and (2) opaque failure modes where request drop rates spike without clear SLO mappings. Current geo-steering policies either over-prioritize latency (causing capacity thrash) or over-prioritize affinity (causing high user-visible errors when local region degrades).

Goals:
- Provide a routing primitive that preserves low-latency affinity for most traffic while allowing controlled, SLO-aware spillover during pressure events.
- Coordinate with circuit breakers and admission controllers so failovers are gradual and observable.
- Offer deterministic knobs for Platform and Dedicated customers: capacity escrow credits, soft-anchor weight, and SLO-weighted hedging.

Proposal summary:
We propose a "Regional Soft Anchor with Capacity Escrow" routing policy (RSA-CE). Key ideas: (a) soft anchors: each request has a probabilistic affinity score to prefer home region while allowing hedging to other regions proportional to spare capacity and SLO slack; (b) escrow tokens: regions maintain a short-lived token pool (capacity escrow) that represents budget available for accepting non-home requests; (c) SLO-weighted steering: routing decisions factor per-region 95th/99th tail headroom (derived from real-time telemetry) so troubled regions export more requests earlier.

Algorithm (high-level):
1. On request arrival, compute home_affinity = base_anchor_weight * session_signal_factor.
2. Query region_state cache: {available_escrow_tokens, token_replenish_rate, slo_slack_percent}.
3. Compute hedging_score = (1 - home_affinity) * f(available_escrow_tokens, slo_slack_percent, latency_bias).
4. If hedging_score > threshold -> select alternate region with highest hedging_score / inverse_estimated_cost.
5. If alternate selected, decrement its escrow token by 1; if no tokens, consult probabilistic fallback that may either queue (if queue depth < Qmax) or attempt best-effort routing according to fallback_policy.

Circuit breaker and load-shedding interactions:
- Circuit breakers mark region state unhealthy when failure rate or queueing latency exceed configured thresholds. RSA-CE treats circuit-open as available_escrow_tokens = 0 and increases slo_slack_percent for the region (so traffic steers away).
- Load shedding is performed at two places: admission controller (reject early when local token exhausted and global capacity is low) and per-region token quota controller (preemptively shed when token burn rate exceeds replenishment by >X%).

SLO mapping and telemetry:
- Map routing decisions to SLOs by computing expected SLO delta per routing action using a simple model: expected_tail_increase = weighted_mean_tail_diff(home_region, candidate_region) * request_cost. 
- Telemetry to capture: token_burn_rate, hedged_request_ratio, rejection_rate_by_region, per-route p50/p95/p99 delta, queue_depth_histograms, circuit_breaker_events, and rollout-tagged user impact.

Configuration knobs (exposed to Console):
- base_anchor_weight (0.0-1.0) default 0.75
- escrow_tokens_per_minute (int) default linked to provisioned RPS & capacity buffer
- token_replenish_policy: time-windowed or EWMA
- slo_slack_thresholds: per-SLO percent windows that trigger more aggressive steering
- hedging_threshold and fallback_policy (reject/queue/best-effort)

Safety and graceful rollback:
- Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% by region with automatic rollback on SLO degradation (preconfigured SLO guardrails: p99 increase > 15% or error-rate increase > 0.5% over baseline).
- Circuit-breaker synergy: when SLO guardrails tripped, temporarily set escrow_tokens to 0 and escalate to traffic-ops channel with automatic mitigation playbook.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for hedging_score math and token accounting (edge cases: negative tokens, rapid replenish, clock skew).
- Integration tests: multi-region simulator that replays live request traces with synthetic region degradations (CPU stalls, kernel flaps, network egress loss).
- Chaos experiments: induce gradual capacity loss in Region A and ensure progressive, observable hedging into Region B with no sudden spike in B's p99.

Rollout milestones and acceptance criteria:
- Stage 1: Implement RSA-CE in routing service (internal feature flag). Acceptance: synthetic replay shows hedged ratio increases smoothly and target region p99 delta remains <10%.
- Stage 2: Console knobs + observability panels + automated SLO guardrails. Acceptance: run closed beta with two PLG accounts; SLA metrics remain within baseline.
- Stage 3: Canary + gradual ramp with runtime-1.22 release. Acceptance: no rollback required and incident reduction in cross-region failovers by >40% during induced events.

Open decisions and trade-offs:
1) Token granularity: requests vs. token-per-kB (we default to per-request tokens but might migrate for embedding-heavy workloads).
2) Centralized vs local token allocator: centralized allocator simplifies global view but is a latency and single-point-of-failure risk; local allocator with gossip is more complex to implement. Current plan: start with fast in-memory coordinator per routing shard with periodic reconciliation to global controller.
3) Session affinity sources: cookie/session-id vs Authorization token. We need a privacy review for using long-lived IDs across regions.

Risks:
- Mis-calibrated tokens could cause over-sharding of traffic, increasing cross-region egress costs. Mitigation: conservative defaults and cost-awareness in fallback policies.
- Telemetry lag may cause oscillation; mitigate by smoothing (EWMA) and minimum stake holding time for tokens.

Linked artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/RSA-CE+Design
- Simulator + test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/pull/197
- Console dashboard mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRSA-CE-dashboard
- Incident playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Regional+Failover+Playbook

- Observability: add token and hedging metrics to runtime metrics (Sofia)
